entries.answer: Demo Hill Shrine (simulated) opens at 05:00 and closes at 21:00 every day. Darshan runs 05:30 to 12:30 and 15:00 to 20:30. There is a cleaning break from 12:30 to 15:00 when the inner area is closed but the route, rest shelters and meal hall stay open. The last entry to the Queue Complex is at 20:00. Timings can change on festival days; the information counter has the day's board.

Early morning (05:30 to 08:00) and the afternoon after 15:00 are the quietest. Weekends and festival days are busiest, especially 09:00 to 12:00. Staggered slot mode spreads arrivals, so booking a slot is the best way to avoid long waits.

entries.topic: The route and the five stops
entries.answer: The route has five stops in order: Base Camp, River Crossing, Forest Path, Queue Complex and Main Steps, then the shrine. Base Camp is where buses arrive. The whole walk is about 2.4 km, 480 steps and 180 m of climb, and takes about 90 minutes for an average adult with short rests.
Base Camp to River Crossing: about 10 minutes, 500 m on a paved path with about 40 easy steps, and a ramp beside them. Easy, wheelchair friendly.
River Crossing to Forest Path: about 20 minutes, 600 m. A footbridge, then a gentle uphill with about 60 steps. Moderate. Wheelchairs use the side ramp.

Forest Path to Queue Complex: about 30 minutes, 700 m. The steepest stretch, with about 200 steps and two sharp bends. Difficult for elders and people with heart or knee problems: take the rest shelters and rest often. Doli-style assistance is available from Forest Path.
Queue Complex to Main Steps: about 20 minutes, 400 m in a covered, railed queue lane with about 120 steps, moderate. Footwear must be left at the stand before the Main Steps.

In total there are about 480 steps. The hardest part is Forest Path to Queue Complex (about 200 steps, steep). Main Steps to the shrine adds about 60 steps; the rest of the route is flat or gently sloping. Rest shelters are placed every 10 minutes of walking.

At Base Camp: drinking water, toilets, cloak room, information and lost-and-found counter, bus stand and parking, a medical post (first aid) and a free walk-in counter where a volunteer can book a slot for you.
At River Crossing: drinking water, toilets and a rest shelter with benches. Water is boiled and filtered.
At Forest Path: drinking water, a rest shelter, a medical post and the doli-style carrying assistance point. This is the last place for assistance before the steep section.
At Queue Complex: drinking water, toilets, a rest area inside the queue lane, a footwear stand and a cloak room for bags and phones if you prefer not to carry them.
At Main Steps: drinking water, a first-aid post and an information counter. There is no cloak room here, so leave bags at Queue Complex.
Free drinking water is available at all five stops. Carry a reusable bottle and refill it; plastic bottles are not allowed on the route.
Toilets are at Base Camp, River Crossing and Queue Complex. Each has separate ladies, gents and accessible cubicles. There are none between Queue Complex and Main Steps, so go before you climb.

entries.topic: Medical post and what it can treat
entries.answer: Medical posts at Base Camp, Forest Path and Main Steps give first aid, blood pressure and sugar checks, oral rehydration, oxygen for breathlessness, and treatment for cuts, sprains, dizziness and heat exhaustion. Serious cases are sent down by stretcher and ambulance from Base Camp. Tell any volunteer and they will take you there. Bring your own regular medicines.

Rest shelters with benches and shade are at River Crossing, Forest Path, Queue Complex and Main Steps, and about every 10 minutes of walking on the steep part. Resting does not lose your slot as long as you reach the Queue Complex within your slot window.

Wheelchairs are free at Base Camp, and doli-style carrying assistance is available from Base Camp and Forest Path. To request it, tell any volunteer, ask at the information counter, or use the app help button. Assistance is arranged on the spot and no payment is ever needed for the request itself; check the posted board for any official carrier rate. A companion can walk alongside.

entries.topic: Cloak room and what cannot be carried
entries.answer: Cloak rooms at Base Camp and Queue Complex keep bags, phones and valuables free of charge against a token. Not allowed on the route or in the queue lane: plastic bottles and bags, sharp objects, alcohol, tobacco, drones, selfie sticks and large backpacks. Small purses and your regular medicines are fine.
Leave footwear at the stand at Queue Complex, free, against a token. Socks are allowed. The route to Queue Complex can be walked in sturdy sandals or shoes.

The information and lost-and-found counter is at Base Camp and Queue Complex, open whenever the shrine is open. They can announce for a missing person, keep found items, give the day's schedule, and call a volunteer or the medical post. There are no phone numbers to remember: any volunteer in a coloured vest can help, and counters are the contact points.

A free vegetarian meal hall at Base Camp serves from 07:30 to 10:00, 12:00 to 15:00 and 18:00 to 20:30. No ticket or payment is needed. Small paid tea and snack stalls are at Base Camp and River Crossing. Carry glucose or a light snack if you are diabetic.

Simple dormitories and rooms are at Base Camp, first come first served, with a small posted charge for rooms and free dorm beds for those with a booked slot. Staying overnight on the route is not allowed. Ask the information counter at Base Camp.

entries.topic: Transport to and from the base
entries.answer: Buses run between the town and Base Camp every 20 minutes from 04:30 to 21:30. The last bus down leaves Base Camp at 22:00. Parking for cars and two-wheelers is at the foot of Base Camp and fills early on weekends. Private vehicles cannot go beyond Base Camp.

Carry: a refillable water bottle, a small snack, your regular medicines, a photo ID, a small towel, a torch for evenings, and a light rain cover. Leave valuables, large bags and anything plastic at home or in the cloak room.
Wear modest, comfortable clothes that cover shoulders and knees and strong footwear with grip. Carry a light layer: evenings and early mornings on the hill are cool. A cap or scarf helps in the sun.

The route is open until dark with lights at every stop, but the Forest Path stretch is dim after 19:00: carry a torch and walk in a group. Steps get slippery in rain, so go slowly and hold the railing. In the heat of 11:00 to 15:00 drink water at every stop. Evenings can be cool.

entries.topic: No payment is asked for a slot; beware of touts
entries.answer: No payment is ever asked for a slot, a walk-in booking or a place in the queue. Slots are free in the app and at the counters. If anyone asks for money to skip the queue, do not pay: walk away and tell a volunteer or the information counter. Only the posted rates for a wheelchair or doli are official.

No plastic on the route. No photography or video in the inner area and queue lane; photography is fine on the route. Keep the lane moving, do not push, and keep the place clean. Please keep voices low near the shrine.

Elders (65 and above) get a priority lane at Queue Complex and a voice-first app. Take the rest shelters every 10 minutes, use the doli-style assistance for the steep Forest Path stretch, and keep medicines with you. A companion may walk with you. Ask any volunteer for help at any stop.

Children under 5 can be carried in a sling; prams cannot go past Forest Path. Hold hands in the queue lane. Free wristbands with your contact point are given at Base Camp to children so a volunteer can reunite them quickly. Baby feeding and nappy changing rooms are at Base Camp and Queue Complex.

Pregnant women are advised to check with their doctor first, to take the doli or wheelchair assistance for the steep part, and to use the priority lane at Queue Complex. Rest at every shelter and drink water often. Tell any volunteer and they will arrange assistance and take you to the medical post if you feel unwell.

The Base Camp to River Crossing stretch is fully wheelchair accessible and ramps reach Forest Path. Free wheelchairs and doli-style assistance can be requested from any volunteer. Visually impaired and hearing impaired pilgrims get a volunteer escort on request. The app speaks and listens in six languages, so no typing is needed.

Stay calm and stay where you are or go to the nearest stop. Tell the nearest volunteer or go to the information counter at once: they will make an announcement and alert every stop. Give the name, age, clothes and where you last saw the person. Children wearing a wristband are brought to the nearest counter. Do not leave the stop until a volunteer confirms the person is found.

Sit down in the nearest shade or rest shelter, drink water, and tell the nearest volunteer. The medical posts at Base Camp, Forest Path and Main Steps can check blood pressure and sugar and give oxygen. For chest pain, fainting or severe breathlessness, tell a volunteer immediately: they will call the stretcher and ambulance. Do not keep climbing.

If you lose your phone, go to the information counter: your slot is tied to your booking, not the phone, so a volunteer can look it up and re-issue it. Lost items found on the route are kept at the lost-and-found counter at Base Camp. Report a stolen phone to a volunteer or the nearest counter. You do not need to pay anything to get your slot back.

Stay calm, move to the side, and do not push. Call out to the nearest volunteer in a coloured vest. They are trained to guide you and to call the medical post and ambulance. Follow the announcements and the lit exit signs. Do not run.

A slot is a 15-minute window to arrive at your chosen stop. Booking is free and takes one message in your language. Arrive within the window; if you are late, a volunteer at the counter will fit you into the next free window. You can change or cancel your slot by asking the app. One slot per person.

No smartphone? A volunteer at the walk-in counter at Base Camp can book a slot for you, speaking for you in your language. Tell them how many people are with you. It is free, and you hear the slot read back. Walk-in slots count together with app slots.

On very crowded days the system switches to rush mode: slots are staggered, spread across later windows so that everyone still gets one, and the map becomes a lighter version that loads faster. The switch is approved by the duty team through NudgeBee. You may be given a slightly later time, but a slot is guaranteed.

The live crowd strip in the app shows the current waiting time at each stop, updated every few seconds (simulated in this demo). Choose the stop with the shortest wait for your slot, or ask the app for the best stop. Waits are longest at Queue Complex and shortest at Base Camp and River Crossing.

entries.topic: App languages, voice and no smartphone
entries.answer: The app speaks and listens in Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, Hindi and English. Press the big button and talk, no typing is needed, and it reads your slot back aloud. Without a smartphone, ask a volunteer at the walk-in counter, who can use the same voice assistant for you.

entries.topic: Where to get help (counters, not phone numbers)
entries.answer: There is no number to call: ask any volunteer in a coloured vest, or go to an information counter (Base Camp, Queue Complex, Main Steps). The medical posts are at Base Camp, Forest Path and Main Steps. For complaints and suggestions, use the feedback box at the information counter.
Entry, slots, walk-in booking, wheelchairs on request, water, cloak room and the meal hall are free. Donations are voluntary and never linked to a slot. Nobody can sell you a faster slot.
Photographs are allowed on the route and at the stops. They are not allowed in the queue lane or inner area. Please do not film other pilgrims.

entries.topic: How long does the whole visit take?
entries.answer: Plan for about 4 to 5 hours: about 90 minutes of walking up, 1 to 2 hours in the queue depending on the crowd, 30 minutes at the shrine and 60 minutes to walk down. Start early in the day.
